question: What will be the percentage change in the S&P 500 index (^GSPC on Yahoo Finance) from the close on 2026-10-15 to the close on 2026-10-23?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to 100 x (close on 2026-10-23 / close on 2026-10-15 - 1), using daily closes of ^GSPC on Yahoo Finance. If there is no close on 2026-10-23, the last close before it is used.

research:
## 1. Resolution source
- I could not load Yahoo Finance's ^GSPC history page directly because the proxy refused the connection. The closes below come from secondary reports.
- 2026-10-15: The S&P 500 closed at **7,744.06**, up 25.12 points (+0.33%). This is the baseline close. It rebounded after three straight down days. [TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/stock-market-today/stock-market-today-dow-jones-sp-500-nasdaq-updates-oct-15-2026), [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/indices/us-spx-500-historical-data), [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-14/stock-market-today-dow-s-p-live-updates)
- The question resolves on the 2026-10-23 close (a Friday, a normal trading day). The window has 6 trading sessions: Oct 16, 19, 20, 21, 22 and 23.

## 2. Current status
- 2026-10-16 (published that day, but the session closed at 20:00 UTC, after the 18:00 UTC forecast deadline): The S&P 500 fell 84.62 points (-1.1%) to **7,659.44**. The Nasdaq fell 2.1% to 26,140.03 and the Dow fell 0.3%. Chipmakers dropped for an 8th straight day, their longest slide since 2008, on worries that AI spending won't pay off. The S&P lost 1.9% for the week. [ABC/AP](https://abcnews.com/Business/wireStory/major-us-stock-indexes-fared-friday-10162026-137331951), [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/markets-news-oct-16-2026-103800633.html), [TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/stock-market-today/stock-market-today-dow-jones-sp-500-nasdaq-updates-oct-16-2026)
- If those figures are right, the index was already about **-1.09%** from the baseline after the first of the six sessions. Nothing settles the question yet.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-16: The AI and semiconductor sell-off deepened, and "bubble" worries grew. Small caps (Russell 2000) and the Nasdaq led the losses. [TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/stock-market-today/stock-market-today-dow-jones-sp-500-nasdaq-updates-oct-16-2026)
- 2026-10-15: The Dow edged higher as tech selling eased, and the S&P gained 0.33%. [TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/stock-market-today/stock-market-today-dow-jones-sp-500-nasdaq-updates-oct-15-2026)
- 2026-10-14: September CPI came in hot: +0.6% m/m and 3.7% y/y, with core also above forecast. Traders started pricing the chance of a Fed rate *hike* at the October meeting. The S&P fell about 1.1% to 7,718.94, its third straight loss and the end of its longest run without a 1% drop in more than six years. A chip-giants gauge fell 4.3%, hit by Micron, Nvidia and Broadcom. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/nasdaq-s-p-500-fall-for-third-straight-session-following-hot-cpi-data-ce785dd2d08bf622), [BBN Times](https://www.bbntimes.com/financial/s-p-500-drops-to-7-718-94-as-hot-september-cpi-and-chip-selloff-hit-wall-street), [Stocktwits](https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/s-and-p-500-nasdaq-see-worst-day-in-over-two-months-as-chipmaker-rout-deepens-cpi-data-comes-in-hot-aapl-spcx-dram-soxx-in-focus/cZxWQBlRBqs)
- Mid-October 2026: Oil prices were high and rising, which added to inflation worries. The Nasdaq's worst week since June was blamed partly on oil. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/15/stock-market-today-live-updates.html)

## 4. Base rates
- These are general historical patterns, not taken from a specific source in this research: over 6 trading days, S&P 500 moves have a standard deviation of roughly 2 to 2.5%. About two thirds of such windows land within about ±2.3%, and moves beyond ±5% are rare (a few percent of windows), usually during crises.
- Rough scaling: an implied volatility (VIX) of about 20 means a weekly standard deviation of about 20/√52 ≈ 2.8%. I could not find a VIX close for 2026-10-15 or 10-16 dated on or before 10-16.
- Average drift is slightly positive, about +0.15% per week.
- Recent behavior: the index went from about 7,811 (implied by the -152.10 weekly change) to 7,659 in the week ending Oct 16. That week had two daily moves of about 1.1%, so realized volatility was above normal.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Kalshi, Polymarket or Manifold market for the S&P 500 close on Oct 23, 2026. Kalshi does run daily and weekly S&P contracts (KXINX series), but I could not get prices.
- 2026-10-16: A Kalshi year-end 2026 contract showed about an 84% chance the index finishes above 7,200 on Dec 31. [next.io/Kalshi references](https://next.io/prediction-markets/trending/what-will-be-the-sp-close-price-end-of-2026/)
- I found no expert forecasts aimed specifically at this one week.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution (Oct 16 to 23)
- A heavy earnings week of about 70 companies. Week-ahead previews were published after Oct 16 (Oct 18 or later, so outside the cutoff); I am listing only the scheduled dates. [CNBC preview](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/18/meta-tesla-netflix-earnings-preview.html), [StockTitan calendar](https://www.stocktitan.net/articles/earnings-calendar-week-of-october-19-2026)
  - Netflix: Tue Oct 20, after the close.
  - Tesla and Meta: Wed Oct 21, after the close.
  - Also reporting that week: IBM, Texas Instruments, Lam Research, SAP, Procter & Gamble, GE Aerospace. The chip names among them (TXN, LRCX) matter given the semiconductor sell-off.
- The Fed meeting ends Oct 28, after the window. However, after the hot CPI, Fed speakers' comments on a possible hike could move markets during the week.
- Other swing factors: oil prices and Middle East supply news, Treasury yields, and whether the chip losing streak continues or reverses.

**Summary:** I couldn't fetch the resolution data directly. Secondary sources put the Oct 15 baseline at 7,744.06. The Oct 16 close of 7,659.44 puts the index about 1.1% below that with five sessions left. That close came after the forecast deadline. Volatility is high because of the hot CPI, a rising chance of a Fed hike, the chip sell-off and high oil, and the window includes a heavy megacap earnings week.
